newsitem.title: CHINA: HORSE RACING-HK ARRESTS FOUR IN RACE-FIXING PROBE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-HK ARRESTS FOUR IN RACE-FIXING PROBE.

text.p: Anti-graft police probing a Hong Kong horse racing scam said on Wednesday they had arrested a businessman on charges of bribing jockeys to fix race results and detained three other suspects.
The arrests added a new twist to the territory's biggest alleged horse race-fixing scandal in a decade.

The drama began in March when the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) hauled away 39 people, including prominent trainers and jockeys, in a swoop by 200 officers at the Sha Tin track on race day.

Ng Siu-chau, a 33-year-old businessman, appeared in court on Wednesday and was charged with offering HK$1 million (US$129,000) in bribes to three apprentice jockeys to pull their horses in a race, an ICAC spokeswoman said.
Ng was remanded in custody until Friday pending further inquiries, she said.
The spokeswoman could not give details of any charges that might be laid against the other three people in ICAC custody, including two jockeys.
The ICAC said the money was intended "as an inducement to or reward for the three apprentice jockeys preventing the horses they were assigned to...from finishing first, second and third".
Ng, 33, was among the 39 people rounded up in March.
In court with five other suspects in June, he was charged on two counts of betting with illegal bookmakers and had been awaiting an August 14 trial on those charges when he was arrested again.
The ICAC said its investigation would continue "with the full support and involvement of the Hong Kong Jockey Club".
In March when the scandal first broke into the open, the Jockey Club suspended two star trainers and five jockeys.
In Hong Kong, punters can only lay their bets legally with outlets of the Hong Kong Jockey Club, which enjoys a monopoly.
The races are the only legal outlet for a flutter for the territory's gambling-mad, predominantly Chinese population, apart from a journey to the casinos of nearby Macau.

Horse racing is a huge industry in Hong Kong, outperforming some weighty blue chip companies in turnover. The money laid on a single race can often exceed the amount gambled on horse racing in many countries in an entire year.
The Jockey Club rang up a betting turnover of HK$92.8 billion (US$12 billion) in the 1996/97 season.
The stakes can be high. After a winner-less jackpot had been carried over from previous race meetings, the 1996/97 season ended last month with a record US$92 million payout to punters.
